bluf: Artefact is a Paris headquartered data and AI consultancy with offices listed from Berlin to Brazil, selling enterprise AI transformation from strategy to deployment and claiming 1,000+ clients. Through 2026 the record shows it buying and hiring outward: Anthropic and OpenAI partnerships, the Explorate AI, Agilytic and Nunatak deals, new chief executives for the UK, Germany and Brazil, a Saudi AI school and, in September 2026, GetMint at the core of its AI Search offer. Horus reads it Favored at 32.6; Monsoon reads Onshore wind at 57.6 with a Brazil hub observed. What a rival should know: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt.
doing:
The positioning line, "Global data and AI consulting company taking clients from strategy to deployment: AI and data transformation, platforms, governance, analytics, data marketing, CX and digital media," decodes to a consultancy that sells the AI programme itself and treats media as one application of the data it builds. The headline claim of "1,000+ clients, including 300 international brands" is quoted as a claim; the record lists 20 clients with evidence.

The sold mix leads with AI Automation / Agents and Data & Measurement, both scored 3: AI headlines the title and H1, GenAI factory and agentic lines sit in the services list, the Bpifrance and Carrefour agentic AI cases carry the evidence, and the data line runs MMM, testing and attribution, CDP and data platform services. AI Search / GEO, Paid Search, Programmatic & CTV, Retail Media and SEO each score 2, with GetMint, German SEA and SEO ads, GMP and Amazon DSP reseller status and the Accor, Deezer, Nissan, TF1 and Unilever cases as evidence. Proprietary lines: the SKAFF platform, the Artefact Research Center, the GenAI Academy, the Data Factory methodology and the Audience Engine.

Its AI posture is end to end enterprise AI transformation: GenAI and agentic factories, AI search via GetMint, the Adopt AI summit at the Grand Palais.

Moves in date order: June 2026, teamed up with Anthropic; July 2026, OpenAI services partner status, the Explorate AI and Agilytic acquisitions, and Athena Vooght appointed chief executive of Artefact UK; September 2026, the Artefact School of AI & Data launched with Saudi Arabia's IT ministry, Stanislas Guerini joined as managing partner for AI transformation, Nunatak joined with Robert Jacobi as CEO for Germany, Rafael Melo appointed CEO of Artefact Brazil, and the GetMint partnership.

The record lists no pricing model. Absent from the record: CRO, Web & Product, Creator & Influencer and Local all score 0, and no case study title names MMM, testing or attribution.
clients:
The ICP is enterprise; the verticals run from FMCG, Retail and Luxury & Beauty through Financial Services, Healthcare, Manufacturing, Telecommunications and Public Sector; the home market is France, with offices from Berlin to Brazil on the record.

Of 20 clients on record, 18 are observed through case studies, 2 names only. AI dominates: 13 of the 20 carry N9, a 0.646 share, against 4 paid performance (N2), 4 local and lead generation (N10), 2 organic (N1), 2 brand (N3) and 1 commerce (N7). The signals: Bpifrance deployed agentic AI across 500 employees with Artefact and Dust; Carrefour, agentic AI for store openings; Bouygues Telecom, an agentic sales assistant; Groupe Barrière, generative agents; Nexans, a 2028 roadmap on Databricks; Vinci Airports, AI with Google Cloud (N9, N3); Ardian, Burger King, Lagardère Travel Retail and Riyadh Air are N9 as well. Accor came for SEO to GEO visibility (N9, N1, N3); Deezer for Performance Max, +28% subscriptions (N2); Reckitt for media spend (N2); TF1 for data collaboration (N2); Unilever for retail media (N10, N2, N7); Nissan for total search efficiencies (N1, N10); Orange for visual recognition AI and L'Oréal for AI trend detection (both N9, N10). FDJ United and Heineken are coded N0, names only.

The shared count is 9: L'Oréal (publicis-sapient, socially-powerful), Orange (semetis, bluerank), Accor (eskimoz), Carrefour (publicis-sapient), Bouygues Telecom (fifty-five), Deezer (phiture), Heineken (the-goat-agency), Nissan (publicis-sapient) and TF1 (click-consult) sit on other tracked books.

The edition's judgments frame what the base needs next: KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) is its strongest tailwind, so these clients will very likely keep buying agent deployment from it; the open question is KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two), where its media clients likely need programmatic and paid social depth it scores at 2 and 1 (moderate confidence).
house: Say and do: AI Search / GEO is contradicted, since it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt while its sitemap holds 21 AI topic URLs, the one gap the Radar flagged; no AI crawlers are listed as blocked. Paid Search is corroborated: the Transparency Center shows 44 Google ads, 15 in the last 30 days, last shown 2026-09-27, under advertiser entities including Artefact Germany GmbH and Artefact Data Spain, S.L.; the samples are German SEO and SEA lines such as "Wir steigern Ihre organische Sichtbarkeit durch datengetriebenes SEO." LinkedIn shows 19 company page ads and 1 thought leader ad (137 ads match the name query, so 20+ is a floor). Publishing cadence is corroborated: 55 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days, 240 in 365, from 1668 URLs. The tag stack is gtm alone on WordPress; no social pixels, test tools or ABM stack show, which is thin for a house that sells CDPs and attribution.
market:
Horus reads Artefact at a tailwind index of 32.6, band Favored, 16:04 on the Solar Arc, say/do integrity 66.7. Best placed for KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), net 0.439, driven by AI Automation / Agents and Data & Measurement. Most exposed to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two), net 0.101 against, driven by Programmatic & CTV and Paid Social. Best scenario fit: The Bazaar of Agents at 45/100. Moves: making P4 (inputs for automation) and P6 (agent operators); partial on P1, P2 and P7 (audited AI visibility, feeds and entities, owned audience hedges); absent on P8 (ads inside assistants); P5 unknown; P3 not applicable.

Monsoon reads 57.6, band Onshore wind: migration 69.6 against displacement 45.6. The sold mix supplies 46 of the index, SEO (9) and Data & Measurement (7) carrying the most movable hours; the footprint is observed, a hub office in Brazil and hub jobs (12 points each), with the work going 37% to South and Southeast Asia and 38% to Africa and the Maghreb. No onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the say/do gap on AI search: it sells AI visibility and holds 21 AI topic URLs, yet publishes no llms.txt and shows no audited citation share or scorecard product (P1 partial). A rival arriving with the audited number and its own llms.txt very likely wins the first conversation with an Accor type buyer (high confidence). The falsifier: an llms.txt on artefact.com or a named AI visibility scorecard at the next compile.

The book is contestable at its media edge, not its AI core: Deezer (phiture), TF1 (click-consult), Reckitt and Unilever came for paid performance and retail media, where it scores 2, and L'Oréal and Orange already shop across publicis-sapient, socially-powerful, semetis and bluerank, so those accounts are likely open to a specialist media pitch (moderate confidence). P8 is absent, so the first agency to show results from ads inside assistants sets the price.

The record lists no pricing model (P5 unknown), so an outcome priced offer meets no public answer, but displacement reads 45.6 and a pure offshore undercut is unlikely to move enterprise clients; the observed Brazil hub gives an onshore delivery pitch something concrete, with roughly an even chance of mattering.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would confirm the KJ6 tailwind Artefact rides and put its unknown pricing model under pressure.
I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, December 2026 to January 2027: disclosed AI checkout GMV strengthens KJ4, while high Shopify opt out rates would slow it.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and raises the value of the GetMint line.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

The GetMint partnership dated September 2026 is the move to follow up: whether an audited AI visibility product or an llms.txt appears on artefact.com by the next Radar compile (the dossier is only as fresh as 2026-09-28).
